meta.title: Ransomware — Finance file server (Akira)
meta.narrative:
At approximately 06:42 on 20 July, the SOC received multiple EDR alerts for mass file encryption on FIN-SRV-02, the primary finance file server. Encrypted files carried the .akira extension and akira_readme.txt ransom notes were dropped across accessible shares, each referencing a unique victim code and a .onion negotiation portal. Tradecraft is consistent with the Akira ransomware operation (RaaS; assessed code lineage to Conti), matching the profile in CISA advisory AA24-109A.

Initial access was via the SSL VPN using valid credentials for a contractor account with no MFA enforced, first used from an anomalous hosting ASN at 02:14 — Akira's most commonly observed entry vector. The actor performed discovery with Advanced IP Scanner and ADFind, harvested credentials from LSASS on a domain-joined host, and created a new domain administrator account named 'itadm' for persistence, a known Akira naming convention. AnyDesk was installed on FIN-SRV-02 to provide a resilient remote access channel.

Approximately 340GB of finance data was staged with WinRAR and exfiltrated using Rclone to a cloud endpoint prior to encryption, consistent with Akira's double-extortion model. Immediately before deployment, volume shadow copies were deleted via PowerShell to inhibit recovery. Containment was achieved by 11:20 through isolation of the affected segment, disabling of the compromised contractor account and the attacker-created itadm account, and removal of the AnyDesk agent.
meta.systems: FIN-SRV-02 (finance file server), FIN-SRV-01 (finance app server), SSL VPN concentrator, DC-01 (domain controller — LSASS credential exposure)
meta.containment: Affected finance VLAN isolated at switch; contractor VPN account disabled and attacker-created 'itadm' domain admin account disabled and preserved for evidence; AnyDesk agent removed from FIN-SRV-02; MFA enforced on all VPN accounts; outbound Rclone/Mega destinations blocked at the perimeter; forced credential reset for accounts exposed via LSASS.

govern.assets: FIN-SRV-02 (finance file server), FIN-SRV-01 (finance app server), VPN concentrator, DC-01 (domain controller — credential exposure suspected)
govern.dataTypes: Employee PII, payroll records, supplier bank details, financial statements
govern.legalNotes: Privilege asserted over IR investigation via external counsel. Do not circulate technical findings outside the response team without legal review.
govern.secureComms: Signal group 'IR-014 Bridge'; encrypted email list ir014@
govern.bizImpact: Finance operations halted ~2 days. Payroll run at risk. Estimated direct cost £180k-£240k including IR retainer, overtime, and restoration. Recovery from backup required as no decryptor is available for current Akira variants.
govern.repRisk: High — supplier bank details exposed; potential media interest if data surfaces on leak site.
govern.insurance: Cyber policy CYB-88213 (Beazley). Notified 28 June. Excess £50k.
govern.riskNotes: Akira operates a Tor-based data-leak site and a double-extortion model. Ransom note contains a unique victim code and .onion portal; no ransom figure is disclosed until the victim initiates contact. 340GB of finance data assessed as exfiltrated and at risk of publication.

custody.notes: Imaged with Tableau write-blocker; hash verified against source.
Copied to evidence NAS (encrypted). Original image sealed in evidence locker E-14.
Captured with WinPMEM prior to isolation to preserve volatile artefacts.
Handed working copy to external IR for malware analysis under NDA/privilege.

iocs.notes: Source of the first unauthorised SSL VPN login using valid contractor credentials with no MFA. Hosting-provider ASN. Matches Akira's primary observed entry vector (CISA AA24-109A).
Compromised contractor VPN account used for initial access. Valid credentials, MFA not enforced.
Attacker-created domain administrator account. 'itadm' is a documented Akira naming convention for persistence accounts.
Akira ransom note dropped in every encrypted directory. Contains a unique victim code and .onion negotiation URL; no ransom figure stated until contact is made.
Extension appended to all encrypted files. Akira uses hybrid ChaCha20 + RSA encryption with partial encryption by file type/size.
Akira Windows encryptor binary recovered from C:\ProgramData. Deletes volume shadow copies before encrypting.
Rclone staged in C:\ProgramData and used to transfer ~340GB of WinRAR-archived finance data to cloud storage prior to encryption. Standard Akira exfiltration tooling.
External endpoint receiving ~340GB outbound over encrypted transport during the pre-encryption staging window.
Legitimate remote access tool installed by the actor as a resilient C2 channel. Named in CISA AA24-109A as standard Akira tooling.
Staging/C2 domain resolved by FIN-SRV-02. Registered three days before the incident.
Credential-dumping tool (Mimikatz-class) detected in memory. Used to harvest domain credentials from LSASS prior to lateral movement.
Network scanning utility used for host and share discovery shortly after initial access. Commonly observed in Akira intrusions alongside ADFind.
Volume shadow copy deletion executed immediately before encryption to inhibit local recovery. Documented Akira behaviour.

actions.title: Isolate FIN-SRV-02 and affected finance segment
actions.notes: Network isolation applied at switch. Segment VLAN quarantined.

actions.title: Disable compromised accounts (svc-contractor01 + reset exposed domain creds)
actions.notes: Contractor account disabled; forced reset of 40 potentially exposed domain accounts.

actions.title: Rebuild FIN-SRV-02 from clean backup and validate
actions.notes: Restoring from 26 June backup (pre-compromise). Validation checklist to follow before return to prod.

actions.title: Enforce MFA on all VPN accounts (close entry vector)
actions.notes: MFA now mandatory on VPN. Contractor access policy under review.

actions.title: Twice-daily executive situation briefing
actions.notes: Ongoing while incident is live. 09:00 and 16:00.

actions.title: Monitor Akira leak site for data publication
actions.notes: Check the Akira .onion leak site daily for signs of the exfiltrated finance data being posted.

escalations.reason: Confirmed data exfiltration (~340GB finance data incl. PII) prior to encryption — elevates from high to critical given regulatory and reputational exposure.

notifications.basis: Art. 33 UK GDPR — 72h from awareness of breach
notifications.notes: Personal data breach affecting employee and supplier PII. Initial notification filed.
Verbal briefing at 07:20, formal escalation follow-up.

notifications.basis: Preserve legal privilege — notify before external comms
Policy obligation — notify within 24h of major incident
notifications.notes: Claim reference CYB-88213 opened. Mandiant engaged via panel.
Pending legal sign-off on wording before sending.

rootCauses.detail: Contractor VPN account permitted single-factor authentication, allowing use of stolen credentials from an anomalous location. VPN access without MFA is Akira's most frequently observed initial access vector per CISA AA24-109A.
rootCauses.remediation: MFA now enforced on all remote access. Contractor accounts moved to time-boxed, MFA-mandatory access with quarterly review.

rootCauses.detail: Once on the VPN segment, RDP to the finance server was unrestricted, enabling rapid lateral movement with harvested credentials.
rootCauses.remediation: Network segmentation project prioritised; RDP restricted to jump hosts with MFA and logging.

rootCauses.detail: Large outbound transfer (~340GB) was not alerted on in near-real-time; discovered during post-incident netflow review.
rootCauses.remediation: DLP egress monitoring and volume-based alerting to be implemented on perimeter.

notes.cl10: Rebuild in progress on FIN-SRV-02 — see action act-003.
notes.cl7: Disk image and memory capture sealed in evidence locker E-14; working copies encrypted on evidence NAS.
